clue.text: I park crookedly behind father to obtain some pepper

indicators.note: behind places the reworked letters after the word for father

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: crookedly says the letters of I and park are set out of line, rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver parks badly behind Dad's car on a trip to buy a spice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crookedly' rearranges I PARK into RIKA, which 'behind' places after PA.
explanation.definitionFit: Paprika is a mild red powder ground from sweet capsicum, a kind of pepper.

clue.text: Stupid person, some say, to hand pie over

indicators.note: over in the sense of knocked over, so the letters of hand pie tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone suggests passing a pie across the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' rearranges HAND PIE; 'some say' softens the insult in the definition, not a sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimwit is called a pinhead, as if their brain were tiny.

clue.text: Tactless way of testing the bath water

explanation.surface: A guide to bathing that also comments on awkward manners.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a blunder in speech, and literally describes dipping a toe or foot into a filled tub.

clue.text: See 2
Use oath in way that's godless

indicators.note: taken as 'in a different way', telling us the letters of use oath are rearranged

explanation.surface: Swearing in a manner that shows no belief in a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheous is a rare word for atheistic, lacking belief in any deity.

clue.text: Cattle twitch caused by motion

parts.note: kine is an old plural for cows or cattle
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A cow jerks nervously as something moves past.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinetic energy is the energy a body has because it is moving.

clue.text: Sauce vessel is in a higher position

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
up means raised or above

explanation.surface: A gravy boat has been placed on a high shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomato condiment is a familiar table relish.

clue.text: No-one from France came up, not being upper class

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the French word for one is read backwards

parts.note: un is French for one

explanation.surface: Nobody arrived from France, as none were posh enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came up' turns UN to NU after NO. NON-U was a 1950s British label for speech and habits judged not upper class.
explanation.definitionFit: The label marked usage thought vulgar by the gentry, the opposite of U (upper-class).

clue.text: Slim had been floored when there weren't many about

parts.note: slim means thin
someone floored is knocked down, on the ground

explanation.surface: A slender boxer was knocked down in a quiet arena.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something scarce, with few examples around.

clue.text: Got acne from one of the same family

indicators.note: from here means made out of, so the letters of got acne are reworked

explanation.surface: A teenager caught spots from a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A cognate is a relative by blood, sharing a common ancestor.

clue.text: Despite that isn't resisting

parts.note: isn't means is not
withstanding means holding out against

explanation.surface: Someone yields even though they claimed not to be resisting.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition means in spite of, regardless of.

clue.text: Lake one had gone into before

indicators.note: the numeral one has gone into the old word for before

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone had waded into the lake earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: One of North America's Great Lakes.

clue.text: One who soundly ridicules coffee

indicators.note: soundly means by its sound, so the word for a scoffer is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: one who ridicules is a mocker

explanation.surface: A thorough critic sneers at a cup of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One who ... ridicules' gives MOCKER; 'soundly' says it is heard, giving a word that sounds the same to a non-rhotic British ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine coffee named after the Yemeni port.

clue.text: Deep sleep 11 (not hot) could produce?

indicators.note: could produce means the remaining letters may be rearranged into something new
not says the abbreviation for hot is to be left out

parts.note: the clue at 11 across gives the coffee word
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A cold coffee might send you into a deep sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes H from MOCHA, leaving MOCA, which 'could produce' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A coma is a prolonged state of unconsciousness.

clue.text: Not so many sheep in France

indicators.note: in puts the female sheep inside the abbreviation for France

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: There are fewer sheep grazing in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Fewer is the comparative of few, meaning a smaller number of.

clue.text: Theatre-in-the-round?

parts.note: a famous London playhouse with a circular plan, and also anything spherical

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's playhouse on the Thames was the Globe, and a globe is a round body.

clue.text: Wander from decapitated animal dunderhead replaced

indicators.note: decapitated means the animal's first letter, its head, is taken off
replaced says a new head goes on where the old one was, a swap of letters

parts.note: a tigress is a female big cat
the head, or first letter, of dunder

explanation.surface: A beheaded beast has a fool's head swapped onto it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitated' takes T off the front of TIGRESS and 'replaced' puts D, the head of dunder, in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress from a topic is to stray away from it.

clue.text: Allowed to twist tape round the little board

indicators.note: round puts the reworked tape around the word for allowed
to twist the tape is to rearrange its letters

parts.note: taken as written
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Permission to wrap tape around a small board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to twist' turns TAPE into PATE, and 'round' splits it to go around LET.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist mixes paint on a small hand-held board.

clue.text: Article removed from stanza ie could be the most comical

indicators.note: could be says the remaining letters are rearranged
removed from says the article comes out of the given letters

parts.note: taken as written
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Dropping one word from a verse might make it funnier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed from' takes one A out of STANZA IE, and 'could be' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Zany means comically eccentric; its superlative means funniest.

clue.text: Full of relish or orange peel, say

definitions.text: Full of relish or orange peel, say

parts.words: Full of relish or orange peel, say
parts.note: keenness and grated citrus rind share one word, and being full of it describes eager enjoyment

explanation.definitionFit: Zestful means enthusiastic and full of gusto; zest is also grated citrus rind.

clue.text: Catchy air precedes outbreak of flu

indicators.note: precedes puts the melody before the rest

parts.note: an air is a melody

indicators.note: an outbreak scatters the letters of flu into a new order

explanation.surface: A song is heard just before a flu epidemic.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodious song is easy to remember.

clue.text: National theme

explanation.definitionFit: A national of a country is a citizen of it, and the topic under discussion is the matter in hand.

clue.text: Destructive good-looker

explanation.walkthrough: SMASHER is British slang for a very attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: One who wrecks things breaks them to pieces, and British slang praises an attractive person as a stunner.

clue.text: Try girl in the factory

indicators.note: in puts the girl inside the word try

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman tries for a job at the works.
explanation.definitionFit: A tannery is a works where hides are processed into leather.

clue.text: Something to wear that's in the window

explanation.definitionFit: A band of cloth worn over the shoulder or waist, and the sliding frame of a British-style window.

clue.text: One legally related?

parts.note: a relative by marriage, whose kinship exists only by legal tie

explanation.definitionFit: A relation by marriage is related by law rather than blood.

clue.text: Boy holds race starter's gun

indicators.note: holds means the boy's name wraps around the letter

parts.note: Ben is a boy's name

indicators.note: the starter of race is its first letter

explanation.surface: A lad keeps hold of the pistol that begins the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts R, the first letter of race, inside BEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bren was a British light machine gun of the Second World War.

clue.text: Relative on British Rail, Eastern Region

parts.note: ER was the abbreviation for British Rail's Eastern Region

explanation.surface: A relative travels on the old British railway network.
explanation.walkthrough: British Rail was the former national railway; the Eastern Region was one of its divisions.
explanation.definitionFit: Brer is a dialect form of brother, as in the folk tales of Uncle Remus.

clue.text: Hack the meat

explanation.definitionFit: To cut with a blow, and a cut of pork or lamb on the bone.

clue.text: Cross it going from one party to another

definitions.text: Cross it going from one party to another

parts.words: Cross it going from one party to another
parts.note: an MP who changes sides is said to cross this space in the Commons chamber

explanation.definitionFit: In Parliament, defecting MPs are said to cross the floor between the facing benches.

clue.text: Left one time with real trouble coming from the side

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: trouble suggests disturbing the letters of real into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone left late and had real trouble on the sidelines.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral means relating to the side, sideways.

clue.text: Hit lazily but hurriedly

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
idly means lazily

explanation.surface: A lazy batsman nonetheless strikes the ball quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapidly means quickly, with haste.
